claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is single-phase, conventionally processed, and has a standard grain size.
A controlled heat treatment can induce dual-phase precipitation in CoCrFeNi.
The proposed treatment will create an ultrafine-grained matrix uniformly containing nanoscale carbide or intermetallic precipitates.
Coupled ultrafine grains and nanoprecipitates constitute a nanohierarchical wear-resistant microstructure.
The nanohierarchical microstructure can evolve during high-temperature sliding to form a dense protective nanocrystalline glaze layer.
At low temperatures, the ultrafine grain structure increases hardness and thereby minimizes adhesive wear.
At high temperatures, the nanoprecipitates oxidize in a controlled manner to generate the glaze layer.
The high-temperature glaze layer is lubricious and reduces friction, adhesive wear, and oxidative wear.
Sequential activation of low-temperature deformation protection and high-temperature glaze protection provides adaptive interface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will maintain a coefficient of friction near or below 0.3 throughout the full temperature range.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will maintain wear rates on the order of 10^-7 mm^3/N·m throughout the full temperature range.
The modified alloy will have lower friction and wear than conventionally processed CoCrFeNi lacking the induced nanohierarchical microstructure.
The proposed operating boundaries are approximately 25–800 °C, ambient air, and moderate-to-high sliding loads.
Excessive precipitate content may cause low-temperature brittleness.
A treated CoCrFeNi group and a conventionally processed CoCrFeNi control group will be tested under identical conditions.
Coefficient of friction, wear rate, nanoprecipitate formation, and high-temperature glaze development will be measured.

The hypothesis is falsified if the treated material fails to reduce both friction and wear across the full range, or if the targeted nanohierarchical structure and elevated-temperature glaze are not observed.
